transcription.text: believer. From the very first century, there was a diverse religious movement known as
Gnosticism, whose followers believed that all the spiritual things were good and all
physical things were evil. Because of this belief, they rejected the incarnation of Jesus.
In fact, many early monastics viewed the body as an obstacle to the spiritual life. They
believed that by neglecting the body, they would actually be strengthening their spirit.
This heresy almost split the church over and over again. And I have to admit, there's still
residue impact that lingers in some Christian traditions today. Now, in one of the traditions
that I grew up in, certain scriptures like Proverbs, chapter 31, verse 30, which says
this, "Charm is deceitful and beauty is fleeting, but a woman who fears the Lord will be praised."
1 Peter 3, verses 3-4 which says, "Don't let your beauty consider you."
